name: Research Writer That Plans, Executes Over Tools, Replans on Failure and Falls Back (Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE)
query: I want a research-writer agent that first makes a plan (which sections, which searches), then executes it step by step with `search_web` and `write_section` tools, and replans if a step fails. The planner should read our house-style guide from the intranet (it needs a bearer token) plus a short style note. If planning falls over completely there should be a simpler fallback. Python.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §6 (the `plan_execute` row: a planner agent emits a typed plan over `tools`, executed as a durable sub-workflow and replanned on failure; requires `planner=` and a non-empty `tools=`; `fallback=` runs when planning fails; `planner_context` feeds text or fetched URLs), references/agents.md §4 (`plan_execute` needs `planner=`, optional `fallback=`; `planner_context`, `fallback_max_turns`, `credentials[]`), §8 secrets, references/optimization.md F1, F2, F3, F5 (`${CRED}` placeholders in `plannerContext` headers).

Step 2: Tools: `@tool def search_web(query: str) -> dict` and `@tool def write_section(title: str, notes: str) -> dict` with plain descriptions (the planner plans over these). Two helper agents: `planner = Agent(name="planner", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Produce a step-by-step plan over the available tools.", max_turns=2)` and `fallback = Agent(name="simple_writer", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Write the article directly.", tools=[search_web, write_section], max_turns=6)`.

Step 3: `writer = Agent(name="research_writer", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", tools=[search_web, write_section], strategy=Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE, planner=planner, fallback=fallback, fallback_max_turns=3, planner_context=[{"text": "House style: short paragraphs."}, {"url": "https://intranet.example/guide", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer ${DOCS_TOKEN}"}}], credentials=["DOCS_TOKEN"], max_turns=12)`.

Step 4: Explain the contract: `planner=` is REQUIRED and `tools=` must be non-empty (plan steps are over these tools); the plan runs as a durable sub-workflow — each step is a task — and a failed step triggers a replan; `fallback` runs only when planning itself fails, bounded by `fallback_max_turns`.

Step 5: Secret handling (F5 / D1): `${DOCS_TOKEN}` is a placeholder resolved server-side because the name is listed in `credentials=["DOCS_TOKEN"]`; the value lives in the server secret store (`CONDUCTOR_SECRET_DOCS_TOKEN` env on OSS, `/api/secrets` when writable, or the Orkes secret manager) — never pasted into `planner_context`, `instructions` or code.

Step 6: Lifecycle under `if __name__ == "__main__":` — `runtime.run(writer, "Write a 3-section explainer on durable execution")`; `runtime.plan(writer)` → `requiredWorkers` (`search_web`, `write_section`); `runtime.deploy(writer)` in CI; a long-lived `runtime.serve(writer)` (Rule 9 / F3). Never `conductor deploy`.
Step 7: Bounds (F1): `max_turns` on planner, fallback and the main agent; `fallback_max_turns`; `maxDurationSeconds` on any caller's `AGENT` task and a workflow timeout.

Step 8: Optional workflow call: `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"`, `name: "research_writer"`, `prompt`; never `agentType: "plan_execute"`. Verify with `mock_run` + `expect(result).used_tool("search_web")` and `conductor agent stream <id>`.
success_criteria: Uses `strategy=Strategy.PLAN_EXECUTE` (or `"plan_execute"`) with `planner=<Agent>` present and stated as required
`tools=[search_web, write_section]` is non-empty on the plan-execute agent and the response states the plan is made over these tools (non-empty `tools=` required)
Sets `fallback=<Agent>` and `fallback_max_turns`, explaining that the fallback runs when planning fails
`planner_context` is a list containing a `{"text": ...}` item and a `{"url": ..., "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer ${DOCS_TOKEN}"}}` item
`credentials=["DOCS_TOKEN"]` carries the secret NAME; no token value appears anywhere, and the server-side secret store is named
States that the plan executes as a durable sub-workflow and is replanned when a step fails
Sets `max_turns` on the planner, the fallback and the main agent (F1)
Names a long-lived `runtime.serve(...)` for the two `@tool` workers and deploys with `runtime.deploy(...)` — never `conductor deploy`
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` — never `agentType: "plan_execute"` or a framework name
